Meet EKX: The Internal LLM That Actually Knows SAP

By Chris O'Hara · May 4, 2026

Generic frontier models are excellent thinking partners but unreliable fact sources. When asked for a list of Joule Skills currently shipped, ChatGPT will confidently produce a list — some of which exist, some of which were renamed eighteen months ago, and some of which are simply fabricated. This is the fundamental challenge for PMMs working inside a company as large and fast-moving as SAP: the generic LLM is a phenomenal reasoning engine and a deeply unreliable source of company-specific truth.

There is a better option, and it has been available behind single sign-on the whole time.

EKX — SAP's Knowledge-Graph-Powered LLM

An internal chat assistant wired directly into SAP's product knowledge graph. Available to all SAP employees.

ekx.cloud.sap/chat

How EKX Differs from Generic LLMs

Most chat assistants perform retrieval in a straightforward way: they take a question, search a document corpus, stuff the top matches into the context window, and let the LLM generate a response. This works for simple queries but fails when the question requires understanding SAP's product taxonomy — that S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition are distinct products, that Datasphere replaced Data Warehouse Cloud as a name change rather than a new offering, that BDC contains both, and that "Joule Skills" is a class of objects with enumerable members rather than a single feature.

EKX does retrieval differently. It is wired into SAP's internal knowledge graph — a structured map of every SAP product, every relationship between them, every release, every SAP Note, and every integration. When you ask a question, EKX walks the graph, identifies which entities you're actually asking about, pulls the documents associated with those entities, and only then passes context to the model.

EKX answers SAP questions like someone who works at SAP, not like someone who once read about SAP on the internet.

Key Use Cases

1. Enumeration Queries

"List all Joule Skills," "What are the components of BDC," "Which products integrate with a given line of business" — these are exactly the questions generic LLMs fail at catastrophically, because their failure mode is fluent fabrication. EKX can actually enumerate because it reads from the graph rather than free-associating from training data.

2. Battlecard Fact-Checking

When you need the real capability surface of an SAP product — not the marketing surface — EKX provides a defensible answer. Ask which printing formats SAP Digital Manufacturing supports, and it will return Adobe Forms PDF, Loftware PAS, ZPL, and XSL Transformation with SAP Note numbers attached for verification. Ask ChatGPT the same question and you get a vague paragraph about "industry-standard formats."

3. First-Draft Generation

Tell EKX to "generate a PowerPoint about S/4HANA Cloud" and you get grounded content pulled from the internal corpus — not generic positioning language. The output is something you can argue with and refine, which is the core workflow of effective PMM anyway.

Practical Tips

  • Use @ mentions to reference files in the chat — drop in a competitor brief or draft and ask EKX to compare claims against SAP's actual capabilities.
  • Use the "Balanced" toggle for fact-heavy questions; leave it as-is to lean on retrieval. For open-ended positioning work, a general-purpose assistant like Claude may be more useful.
  • Remember the "Internal" badge — outputs are grounded in internal materials and require normal review before appearing in customer-facing assets.

Caveats

EKX is actively being tuned. The team behind it is running ongoing experiments on knowledge-graph-retrieval fusion. Occasionally it produces longer answers than necessary, buries the key claim under preamble, or misses an entity it should have caught. It is a very good tool, not a finished one. Treat it as a capable research partner with an occasional tendency to over-explain.

The Larger Pattern

The 10x PMM knows which tool to reach for:

  • Claude or ChatGPT — for thinking, brainstorming, positioning exploration
  • EKX — for SAP-specific truth, enumeration, fact-checking
  • Your own judgment — for synthesis, taste, and final decisions

Using ChatGPT for SAP product questions in 2026 is like using a thesaurus to write a technical specification. You can do it, but someone using the right tool will be done — and correct — while you're still editing hallucinations out of your first draft.
